headline: COPPER ERASES NVIDIA REBOUND, HITS 52-WEEK LOW — Bears Reject Relief Rally; $11,700 Now Resistance Not Support
snippet: Copper failed to hold a brief relief rally tied to Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, with the LME price sinking to a fresh 52-week low even as equity markets recovered — a bearish signal that metals investors are treating the AI-driven selloff as a structural repricing rather than a dip. The failed rebound at $11,700 per tonne now converts that level from support to resistance, while Comex copper remains 21% below its September record and Freeport-McMoRan and other majors face continued pressure on 2027 capex decisions. For TSX-V and ASX copper juniors, a commodity now making new 52-week lows despite a positive equity catalyst is the worst possible capital-raising environment heading into year-end.

headline: AUSTRALIA MONTHLY CPI BEATS FORECASTS — Higher-Than-Expected Inflation Sends ASX Lower; Global Rate Hike Fears Deepen
snippet: Australia's October monthly CPI data came in above expectations on November 25, sending the ASX lower at open and reinforcing expectations that the Reserve Bank of Australia may need to hold or hike rates longer than previously anticipated. The hot print compounds the global rate pressure already driving the November precious metals rout — with the US Federal Reserve's December meeting at a 96%+ hike probability and now Australia's data adding a second major developed-market rate hawkishness signal on the same day as the US October PCE release. For ASX-listed gold and copper miners, Australia-specific inflation risk adds a domestic headwind to the global commodity price selloff already under way.

headline: GOLD NEAR 15-MONTH LOW AT $3,550 AS PCE DATA TESTS $3,500 FLOOR — Market Braces for Final Inflation Print Before December FOMC
snippet: Gold hovered near a 14-to-15 month low around $3,550 per ounce as of Wednesday morning, with market attention locked on the October Personal Consumption Expenditures price index — the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge — released later in the day. FXStreet's pre-release analysis identifies $3,500 as the critical technical support level that bulls must defend; a core PCE reading above the expected 3.2% would reinforce the December Fed hike narrative and likely break that floor. With the gold-silver ratio near 85, silver remains more vulnerable than gold to a hot PCE print, as industrial components amplify monetary tightening risk.

headline: COWBOY STATE MINE PFS: $1.3B NPV, 24% IRR AND 116MT RESERVE IN WYOMING — American Rare Earths First US Rare Earth Project to Clear Pre-Feasibility With Declared Reserve
snippet: American Rare Earths (ASX: ARR) has completed a prefeasibility study on its Cowboy State Mine in Wyoming — the first development phase of the larger Halleck Creek project — delivering an after-tax NPV of approximately US$1.3 billion at an 8% real discount rate, an after-tax IRR of 24%, and a maiden Probable Ore Reserve of 116.4 million tonnes grading 1,257 ppm payable rare earth oxide, with a modelled 26-year mine life and commissioning targeted for 2030. Pre-production capital is estimated at US$840 million including contingency. Crucially, the Cowboy State Mine covers less than 5% of the total Halleck Creek resource — leaving the bulk of a potentially tier-one rare earth district for future study phases. For investors evaluating Western rare earth supply chain alternatives to China, a US-jurisdiction PFS with a declared reserve and positive economics at current prices is a meaningful de-risking milestone.

headline: DLP EXPANDS ESPERANZA TO 24,900 HECTARES, IDENTIFIES 2 NEW PORPHYRY TARGETS — Cu-Mo-Au System Now Four High-Priority Targets, 35km from Cerro Verde in Peru
snippet: DLP Resources (TSX-V: DLP) expanded its Esperanza copper-molybdenum-gold project in southern Peru to approximately 24,900 hectares and identified two new porphyry copper-molybdenum-gold targets, bringing the property's total drill-ready target count to four. Esperanza sits approximately 35 kilometres from Freeport's Cerro Verde — one of the world's largest copper mines — and the expansion from earlier claim blocks increases the land package around what management is describing as an emerging district-scale discovery. For TSX-V investors evaluating copper exploration at a time when copper equities are at 52-week lows, district-scale land acquisitions in established mining corridors represent option value that is not dependent on near-term commodity price recovery.

headline: AURIGINAL HITS 54.7m AT 1.21 G/T Au OUTSIDE 1.39 MOZ ROGER RESOURCE — Twice the Deposit Grade; Quebec Gold Extends Beyond Existing Boundary
snippet: Auriginal (TSX-V: AUME) reported that drill hole AUR-26-13 returned 54.7 metres at 1.21 g/t gold at a location outside the boundary of its existing 1.39 million ounce Roger resource in Quebec — grading at more than twice the current resource model's average, which immediately signals a potential grade upgrade in the next resource estimate. Finding bulk-width, above-average grade mineralisation outside the existing resource boundary is one of the more bullish exploration signals a junior can generate, as it suggests the deposit is both larger and higher-grade than the model currently reflects; a 2027 resource update will incorporate 2026 drilling and is the first to include this result.

headline: EMPEROR METALS RETURNS 18.7m AT 3.0 G/T Au AT DUQUESNE WEST — 64 of 77 Holes Assayed; Globex JV Keeps Posting Wide High-Grade in Abitibi
snippet: Emperor Metals — in joint venture with Globex Mining (TSX: GMX) — reported additional assays from Duquesne West in Quebec's Abitibi camp, including 18.7 metres at 3.0 g/t gold from hole DQ 26-55. With assays now returned from 64 of 77 drill holes in the program, the remaining 13 holes represent a material additional data release still to come. Duquesne West sits in the Abitibi Greenstone Belt — the most prolific gold district in Canadian history — and wide intervals averaging 3+ g/t at this stage of a 77-hole program are consistent with the type of continuous mineralisation needed to support a resource of economic interest at junior development grade.

headline: METALSOURCE MINING INTERCEPTS 416 G/T AgEq AT SILVER HILL — New Zone Opens 17.28m South of Existing High-Grade; B.C. Silver Project Extends
snippet: Metalsource Mining (CSE: MSM) reported that hole SH26-27 at the Silver Hill project in British Columbia returned a 17.28-metre mineralised zone including a 3.6-metre interval grading 416 g/t silver equivalent — a bonanza-grade intercept in a wide mineralised package that remains open to the south, the direction of this new discovery. Silver Hill's emerging footprint of high-grade intervals across multiple holes separated by meaningful along-strike distances is exactly the geological pattern that justifies resource definition drilling, and the southward-open geometry means the system boundary has not yet been defined.

headline: US URANIUM OUTPUT PLUNGES 78% IN Q3 2026 AFTER WHITE MESA SUSPENSION — Single Mill's Downtime Erases Three-Quarters of US Production; December Campaign Now Critical
snippet: US uranium production fell 78% in the third quarter of 2026 compared to prior periods, with World Nuclear News tying the collapse almost entirely to the temporary suspension of processing at Energy Fuels' White Mesa Mill in Utah — the only conventional uranium mill licensed and operating in the United States. The concentration of US uranium processing at a single facility has made domestic output extraordinarily sensitive to that one plant's operational schedule, and the Q3 data underlines why Energy Fuels' planned December production campaign targeting 1 million pounds is strategically critical for US utility procurement. For uranium investors, the Q3 production data quantifies the supply gap that domestic mines alone cannot bridge, reinforcing the structural case for elevated long-term contract prices currently at approximately $98 per pound.

headline: SCHAEFFER'S: GOLD MINING STOCK REBOUND SIGNALS HISTORY OF 20% SUCCESS — Technical Pattern Warns November Recovery Could Stall
snippet: Schaeffer's Investment Research flagged on November 23 that a specific technical signal in gold and copper mining stocks — appearing after Freeport-McMoRan and peers posted strong recovery gains — has historically preceded continued strength only 20% of the time one month later, against a broad analyst consensus of 18 of 24 brokerages holding 'buy' or 'strong buy' on Freeport. The analysis challenges the consensus view that the November selloff has created a straightforward buy opportunity, arguing that the signal's poor historical forward returns suggest the bounce may be a relief rally within a larger corrective move rather than the beginning of a sustainable recovery. For retail investors deciding whether to add to mining positions during the November rout, the divergence between analyst ratings and technical signals is precisely the kind of ambiguity that makes position sizing discipline more important than directional conviction.
